title: One Seat, Two Ideas
text: You can sit on a cloud or under the sea. Each choose one. Ask “Why?” Agree where to sit. Write “We choose… because…”

title: Tiny or Giant Lunch
text: Choose a tiny sandwich or a giant grape. Tell your partner why. Ask what they think. Write both choices.

title: A Sound for Monday
text: What sound should start Monday: a bell, a song or a lion? Each choose. Ask “Why?” Write your choices and one reason.

title: Our Invisible Pet
text: Choose an invisible cat or an invisible bird. Ask your partner “What can it do?” Agree. Write your pet and one ability.

title: Pocket Weather
text: You can carry sunshine or snow in your pocket. Explain one use for each. Agree which to keep. Write your choice and its best use.

title: The Extra Button
text: Add one button to a backpack: make it fly or make it find lost things. Each explain a choice. Agree. Write the button and why.

title: Only One Flavour
text: Invent two ice-cream flavours, one each. Ask “Would you try mine?” Choose one to sell. Write its name and ingredients.

title: The Ten-Minute Gift
text: You get ten free minutes. Each suggest an activity. Ask one question about your partner’s idea. Agree on one. Write the plan and why.

title: One Useful Swap
text: Would you swap your voice with a trumpet or your laugh with a drum? Each explain. Write both choices and one possible problem.

title: Keep One Convenience
text: Choose instant drying clothes or never losing keys. Each defend one. Ask “When would that help?” Write your agreement and one drawback.

title: Say My Sandwich
text: Invent a sandwich with three fillings. Tell your partner. They repeat it. Swap. Write your partner’s three fillings.

title: My Made-Up Morning
text: Tell your partner three things an imaginary person does before breakfast. They retell them in order. Swap. Write one person’s three actions.

title: Did You Mean That?
text: Say “The small dog needs a big hat.” Your partner repeats it with one detail wrong. Correct them. Swap with a new sentence. Write one correction.

title: Listen for the Favourite
text: Invent a character. Say their favourite food, colour and animal. Your partner asks one question. Swap. Write your partner’s character and favourites.

title: Three Details, One Robot
text: Describe a robot’s colour, size and job. Your partner repeats the details. Swap. Write one robot description you both checked.

title: Repeat the Plan
text: Plan a pretend visit: a day, a time and an activity. Your partner checks “Did you say…?” Swap. Write one checked plan.

title: Your Idea, My Words
text: Each suggest a way to make waiting less boring. Explain your partner’s idea in your own words. Ask “Is that right?” Write both ideas.

title: One Important Difference
text: Describe two imaginary shoes with one difference. Your partner finds the difference. Swap. Write the two shoes and what is different.

title: Check Before You Promise
text: One asks for help with an imaginary event. The other checks the job and time before agreeing. Swap. Write the checked job, time and agreement.

title: Twenty Words of Advice
text: Each give advice for learning something difficult. Retell your partner’s advice in twenty words or fewer. Ask if it is fair. Submit one checked summary.

title: A Secret Kitchen Thing
text: Think of a kitchen object. Give three clues without its name. Your partner guesses. Swap. Write one object and the clue that helped most.

title: Guess the Strange Job
text: Invent a job for a tiny person. Describe two duties. Your partner guesses the job. Swap. Write one job name and its duties.

title: The Five-Question Fruit
text: Secretly choose a fruit. Your partner asks up to five yes/no questions and guesses. Swap. Write one fruit and two questions you used.

title: Object with No Colour
text: Describe an everyday object without naming its colour or its name. Your partner guesses. Swap. Write one object and two useful clues.

title: A Place in Your Head
text: Imagine a room with three things. Describe the things. Your partner guesses the room. Swap. Write one room and its three things.

title: Animal by Its Problems
text: Choose an animal. Describe two problems it might have, without naming it. Your partner guesses. Swap. Write the animal and its problems.

title: The Missing Verb
text: Say “I can…” and give two clues about the action. Your partner guesses the verb. Swap twice. Write two verbs you guessed.

title: Guess the Impossible Object
text: Invent an object with a surprising use. Explain its size and what it does. Your partner names it. Swap. Write one name and use.

title: Clue Upgrade
text: Choose an object. Give a vague clue, then a better clue. Your partner explains which helps more. Swap. Write the object and both clues.

title: Spot My Secret Rule
text: Choose a word rule, like “things you can eat.” Give three examples. Your partner tests another word and guesses. Write the rule and examples.

title: The Wrong Sandwich Order
text: Pretend one ordered cheese but got tomato. Ask politely for a change. The other replies. Swap. Write the request and reply.

title: Borrow It, Bring It Back
text: Ask to borrow an imaginary umbrella. The owner asks when you will return it. Agree. Swap. Write the request and return time.

title: A Delivery for a Giant
text: One is a giant ordering a chair. The seller asks about size and strength. Agree on a chair. Write its size and one special feature.

title: You Have the Wrong Number
text: Pretend you call a bakery but reach a bicycle shop. Find the mistake politely. Swap. Write a four-line conversation.

title: The Ticket Question
text: One wants a ticket for tomorrow. The seller asks “Morning or afternoon?” Agree on a time. Swap. Write the request and answer.

title: A Robot Customer
text: One is a robot buying a hat. The seller asks two questions. Choose a hat. Swap. Write the hat and why it suits the robot.

title: The Unclear Invitation
text: Invite your partner to an imaginary activity but forget the time. They ask for it. Agree. Swap. Write the complete invitation.

title: Ask for a Quieter Seat
text: Pretend your seat is too noisy. Ask a staff member to move. They offer another seat. Swap. Write the request and solution.

title: Sorry, That Is Sold Out
text: One orders a strawberry drink. It is sold out. The other offers two alternatives. Agree. Swap. Write the alternatives and final choice.

title: A Promise You Can Keep
text: A customer wants a parcel today. The seller can deliver tomorrow. Discuss one helpful alternative. Write the final promise and why it is realistic.

title: Fifteen or Fifty?
text: One says “fifteen tickets.” The other hears “fifty.” Ask “Did you say…?” Clear it up. Swap. Write the corrected number in a sentence.

title: Tuesday Is Not Today
text: One invites a friend for Tuesday. The friend thinks today. Ask questions to fix it. Write the corrected invitation and a checking question.

title: Your Left or Mine?
text: Imagine you face each other. One says “Look left.” Discuss why that is confusing. Write a clearer instruction using an imaginary object as a marker.

title: Which Blue One?
text: Imagine two blue bags: one big, one small. Ask for a bag clearly. Your partner checks. Swap. Write one clear request and reply.

title: Not Angry, Just Busy
text: A short message says “Later.” One thinks it is angry. Discuss another meaning. Rewrite it as a friendly message with a time.

title: Check the Name Twice
text: Invent two similar names. Pretend to book a table. Ask how to spell the right name. Swap. Write the name and a spelling question.

title: Too Hot to Wear
text: One says “That jacket is hot.” Discuss two meanings: warm or stylish. Ask a checking question. Write both meanings and your question.

title: A Better Voice Message
text: Say “Bring that thing at that time.” Your partner asks what and when. Invent the missing details. Write a clear new message.

title: The Joke Did Not Land
text: Invent a harmless joke that could confuse a new learner. Your partner asks what it means. Explain kindly. Write the joke and explanation.

title: Clear Without Being Rude
text: One says “Your idea will never work.” Discuss a kinder way to disagree and ask a question. Write your improved reply.

title: The Shoe That Sneezed
text: Start “My shoe sneezed.” Take turns adding one sentence. Stop after four sentences. Give the story a title. Submit your title and story.

title: A Message in a Biscuit
text: One invents a message inside a biscuit. The other says what happens next. Add an ending together. Write the message and two story sentences.

title: The Lift Goes Sideways
text: Start “The lift went sideways.” Each explain what is outside when it opens. Choose one idea. Write a three-sentence story.

title: One Sock on a Mission
text: A sock wants a new job. Each suggest a job. Choose one and invent a problem. Write the sock’s job, problem and solution.

title: Before the Photo
text: Imagine a photo of a dog wearing a crown. One explains what happened before. The other explains what happens next. Write both parts.

title: The Polite Monster Knock
text: A monster knocks and asks for sugar. One speaks as the monster; one as the neighbour. Write your four-line conversation.

title: Change Only the Ending
text: One tells a three-sentence invented story. The other changes only its ending. Discuss which is better. Write the two endings and your choice.

title: The Accident Was Useful
text: Invent a small accident, like spilling paint. Your partner turns it into something useful. Swap. Write one accident and its good result.

title: Two Sides of a Sandwich
text: A sandwich disappears. One tells the story as the cook; one as the hungry dog. Write both versions and one fact they agree on.

title: A Twist That Makes Sense
text: Invent a surprising ending. Your partner asks what earlier clue would make it fair. Agree. Write the ending and that earlier clue.

title: The Three-Item Picnic
text: Plan a pretend picnic with only three items. Each suggest two. Agree on three. Write your list and one reason.

title: Teach a Robot to Tidy
text: Tell a pretend robot how to tidy a desk. Each suggest a step. Agree on three steps in order. Write them.

title: Our Five-Minute Show
text: Plan a five-minute show using only voices. Each suggest an act. Agree on a beginning and ending. Write the plan.

title: A Break for Both
text: One wants a quiet break; one wants to move. Find a plan that gives both a turn. Write the two activities and times.

title: Pack for a Tiny Guest
text: A tiny imaginary guest is visiting. Each suggest something they need. Choose three things. Write the items and what each is for.

title: Make Waiting a Game
text: Invent a talking game for a ten-minute wait. Explain one rule each. Agree on two rules. Write the rules and how the game ends.

title: The Surprise with No Money
text: Plan a kind surprise for an imaginary friend. It must cost nothing. Ask what your partner can do. Write the plan and each person’s job.

title: A Rainy Plan Switch
text: Plan an outdoor activity. Now imagine rain. Ask your partner for another idea. Agree on an indoor plan. Write both plans.

title: Two Jobs, One Deadline
text: Imagine you must write an invitation and make a guest list before noon. Divide the jobs. Ask “Can you finish by…?” Write your agreement.

title: Our Backup for a Missing Item
text: Plan to teach a simple game. Then remove one useful item. Discuss how to adapt. Write the game, missing item and revised plan.

title: An Alarm for a Snail
text: Invent an alarm for a sleepy snail. Each suggest a sound. Agree on one. Write its sound and what the snail does next.

title: The Helpful Pocket
text: Invent a pocket that does one useful thing. Ask your partner “What can it do?” Agree. Write its name and ability.

title: Shoes for a Cloud
text: A cloud wants shoes. One suggests a material; the other suggests a special feature. Explain both. Write your design.

title: A Mug with a Job
text: Give a mug a second job. Each suggest one. Ask “How would that work?” Choose. Write its new job and how it works.

title: The Tiny Helpful Machine
text: Invent a machine smaller than your hand. Each add one feature. Write what it looks like and what it does.

title: A Snack for Space
text: Invent a snack that will not float away. Discuss its shape and packaging. Write the snack and how people eat it.

title: A Sign with No Words
text: Invent a symbol meaning “Please wait.” Describe it to your partner. They say what it means to them. Improve it. Write the final symbol description.

title: The Polite Doorbell
text: Invent two funny but polite doorbell messages. Say them to each other. Choose one. Write the message and why you chose it.

title: Sell the Almost-Useless Thing
text: Invent an almost-useless object. Your partner finds one real use for it. Discuss who might want it. Write the object, use and customer.

title: Improve One Bad Feature
text: Invent a useful gadget with one annoying feature. Your partner suggests a fix. Agree. Write the gadget, problem and improvement.

title: Our Shared Breakfast Ingredient
text: Each invent a breakfast. Ask what is in your partner’s meal. Find one shared ingredient, or add one together. Write both breakfasts and the shared ingredient.

title: Two Imaginary Bedrooms
text: Each invent a bedroom with three things. Compare. Write one thing both rooms have and one difference.

title: The Same Gift, Different Uses
text: You both receive a large cardboard box. Each explain a different use. Ask one follow-up question. Write both uses.

title: Two Routes to Relax
text: Each invent a relaxing activity for a fictional character. Ask “Why does that help?” Write the activities and one similarity.

title: Which Instructions Help?
text: Compare “Make it nice” with “Add a title and two colours.” Discuss which is easier to follow. Write your choice and why.

title: Our Shared Silly Skill
text: Each invent two silly skills. Find one you would both like. Ask “Why?” Write the skill and one reason from each person.

title: A Bag for Two People
text: One needs a bag for books; one for sports clothes. Compare needs. Design one bag for both. Write two features and their uses.

title: Fast or Careful This Time?
text: Compare packing a lunch and crossing a busy road. Discuss when speed matters and when care matters. Write your advice for each.

title: One Rule, Two Reactions
text: Imagine a club bans all music. Each explain a different reaction. Agree on a fairer rule. Write both reactions and your new rule.

title: Find the Real Disagreement
text: One wants a short meeting; one wants everyone heard. Ask what each really needs. Write a plan that meets both needs.

title: A Helpful First Reply
text: An imaginary friend says “I do not understand the game.” Each suggest a helpful reply. Choose one. Write it and one simple question.

title: Teach Me Your Made-Up Word
text: Invent a word for a useful action. Explain it to your partner. They use it in a sentence. Swap. Write one word, meaning and example.

title: Praise the Effort
text: Imagine your partner tried a difficult puzzle. Give a kind message about their effort. Swap. Write both messages.

title: One Clear Tip
text: One pretends to be learning to cook rice. Ask what is confusing. Offer one simple tip. Swap with another skill. Write one question and useful reply.

title: Let Me Try Again
text: One says “I got it wrong.” The other offers a kind next step. Swap. Write a two-line exchange.

title: Help Without Taking Over
text: Your partner pretends to be stuck writing a title. Ask about their idea. Offer two titles and let them choose. Write the choice and why.

title: A Welcome in Two Lines
text: An imaginary new member joins your club. Each suggest a welcome. Agree on two lines: a greeting and an invitation. Write them.

title: Explain the Button
text: Invent a button for a simple machine. Explain what it does. Your partner asks one question. Improve the explanation. Write the final version.

title: Advice with a Choice
text: An imaginary friend is bored with a hobby. Discuss two options without telling them what they must do. Write both options and a question.

title: Feedback They Can Use
text: Invent a two-line advertisement. Your partner says one strength and one clear improvement. Revise it. Submit the new advertisement and what changed.

title: Three Seats on a Cloud
text: A cloud has room for three imaginary passengers. Each suggest one animal. Explain why it should come. Write your passenger list and one reason each.

title: The One-Shelf Museum
text: Your museum has one shelf. Each suggest an everyday object worth showing. Agree on three objects. Write the objects and what visitors can learn.

title: Ten Coins for Fun
text: Plan fun with ten pretend coins. Games cost four, music three, snacks five, decorations two. Each suggest a plan. Agree. Write your choices and total.

title: The Six-Word Club Motto
text: Each suggest a word for a friendly club. Use everyone’s ideas to make a motto of six words or fewer. Say it together. Write the motto.

title: One Box, Three Essentials
text: An imaginary visitor can bring only three objects. Each suggest one and explain its use. Agree on the list. Write the objects and uses.

title: The Last Free Hour
text: You share one free hour. Each wants a different activity. Divide the time fairly. Ask “Is that enough?” Write the activities and minutes.

title: A Shop with Three Products
text: Invent a shop that sells only three things. Each suggest one. Agree on a shop name. Write the name and the three products.

title: Our Quiet Celebration
text: Plan a celebration with no loud sounds. Each suggest an activity. Choose two. Write the activities and how people show they are happy quietly.

title: Keep Two, Drop One
text: Choose between free snacks, longer breaks and more games for an imaginary club. Each defend one. Keep two. Write your choices and why one was dropped.

title: No Screens, Still Fun
text: Plan entertainment for a screen-free afternoon. Each suggest a different idea. Agree on three activities in order. Write the plan.

title: The Banana on the Bus
text: Start “A banana got on a bus.” Each add one sentence. Together add an ending. Write your short story.

title: Three Strange Deliveries
text: Each invent a strange parcel. Decide why all three arrive at one house. Write the parcels and one explanation connecting them.

title: The World Forgot Socks
text: Imagine nobody remembers what socks are. Each suggest a new use for them. Choose the funniest. Write your chosen use and how people discover the truth.

title: A Door in a Sandwich
text: A sandwich has a tiny door. Each say what could be behind it. Choose one idea. Write three sentences about opening the door.

title: Weather with Feelings
text: One speaks as the sun, one as rain, one as wind. Explain why you are upset. Find a happy ending. Write the problem and solution.

title: The Forgotten Superpower
text: Invent a hero who forgets their power. Each suggest a clue that reminds them. Choose two clues. Write the power and clues.

title: Beginning, Trouble, Fix
text: Invent a lost toy story. One gives the beginning, one the problem, one the fix. Ask questions to connect them. Write the three parts.

title: Same Event, Three Witnesses
text: A cake falls over. Each invent a different explanation. Ask questions. Agree on the most likely story. Write it and one clue that supports it.

title: The Good News Chain
text: Start “The train was late.” Each add an unexpected good result. Connect the results. Write a three-step chain.

title: A Villain Changes Jobs
text: Invent a cartoon villain who wants a helpful job. Each suggest a job using one of their skills. Agree. Write the job, useful skill and first task.

title: A Chair for Everyone
text: Design an imaginary chair. Each name one need: comfort, space or easy movement. Add a feature for each. Write your three features.

title: Our Impossible Umbrella
text: Each add one funny feature to an umbrella. Decide what it looks like. Write its name and three features.

title: The Robot with One Job
text: Each suggest a boring job for a robot. Choose one. Discuss a mistake it might make. Write the job and a rule to prevent that mistake.

title: A Playground on the Moon
text: Each invent one piece of play equipment for low gravity. Ask how it works. Choose two. Write the equipment and how to use it.

title: The Friendly Warning Sound
text: Invent a sound that means “Be careful.” Each suggest one. Choose a sound and a situation. Write what it sounds like and when to use it.

title: The Backpack That Organises
text: Each choose something a backpack often loses. Design a feature for each item. Write three items and how the bag keeps them easy to find.

title: Our Made-Up Sport
text: Invent a sport played only with words. Each suggest a rule. Agree on three rules and how to win. Write them.

title: An Animal-Friendly Machine
text: Choose an imaginary machine that helps animals. Each suggest a feature. Discuss one possible problem. Write its purpose, best feature and a fix for the problem.

title: A New Way to Say Thanks
text: Invent a short phrase that means “Thank you.” Each suggest one word. Combine your ideas. Write the phrase and when people use it.

title: The Invention Test Panel
text: Invent a device that finds lost shoes. One asks about speed, one about cost, one about mistakes. Agree on an improved design. Write its three answers.

title: Too Many Hats
text: A pretend guest owns ten hats but has one head. Each suggest a use for the extra hats. Choose two. Write the uses.

title: The Silent Alarm Clock
text: An imaginary alarm makes no sound. Each suggest another way it could wake someone. Agree on one. Write the idea and why it works.

title: Everyone Wants the Window
text: Three travellers want the window seat. Each suggest a fair solution. Choose one. Write the rule and explain why it is fair.

title: A Very Small Table
text: Three friends have six plates and a tiny table. Each suggest a way to eat together. Agree. Write your solution.

title: The Instructions Blew Away
text: You have an imaginary flat-pack shelf but no instructions. Each suggest a sensible next step. Choose two. Write them in order.

title: A Queue of Impatient Penguins
text: Penguins are waiting for a slide. Each suggest a way to keep the queue fair and fun. Choose two ideas. Write them.

title: Nobody Can Find the List
text: Your pretend club keeps losing its task list. Each suggest a fix. Agree on where to keep it and who checks it. Write the plan.

title: The Giant Whisper Problem
text: A friendly giant whispers very loudly. Each suggest a quiet way for the giant to say hello. Choose one. Write how it works.

title: Two Good Ideas Collide
text: One club member wants surprise events; another needs plans early. Each offer a solution. Agree on a compromise. Write what stays secret and what is announced.

title: The Helpful Machine Is Annoying
text: A machine reminds everyone to drink water every minute. Discuss what helps and what annoys. Agree on a change. Write the problem and improved reminder rule.

title: The Dragon Haircut
text: Choose roles: dragon, hairdresser, friend. The dragon wants a new look. Each ask or answer a question. Agree. Write the haircut and one practical detail.

title: A Table for Three Species
text: Be a mouse, a giraffe and a human choosing a table. Each explain one need. Design a solution. Write how everyone can eat comfortably.

title: The Interviewing Toaster
text: One is a toaster applying for a job. The others ask one question each. Answer as the toaster. Write the job and two answers.

title: A Customer, a Cook, a Translator
text: A customer wants a meal with no onions. The cook misunderstands. A helper explains clearly. Agree on the meal. Write the corrected order.

title: The Lift for a Giraffe
text: Be a giraffe, a builder and a designer. Explain the problem with a normal lift. Agree on a change. Write the change and why it helps.

title: The Missing Parcel Desk
text: Choose sender, receiver and helper. Invent a parcel’s colour and size. Ask questions to identify it. Write its description and the next step.

title: A Tiny Band Interview
text: Two are musicians with imaginary instruments. One is the interviewer. Ask each what they play. Choose a band name together. Write the name and instruments.

title: The Nervous Presenter
text: One is a nervous presenter; two are helpers. Ask what would help. Each offer one idea. Agree on a plan. Write the two helpful ideas.

title: The Customer Wants Everything
text: Choose customer, maker and adviser. The customer wants a bag that is cheap, huge and tiny when folded. Discuss trade-offs. Write an agreed design and limitation.

title: The Honest Advertisement Team
text: Choose inventor, customer and editor. Invent a gadget. The customer questions a big promise; the editor improves it. Write the realistic advertisement.

title: A Mascot Made of Food
text: Each suggest a food as an imaginary team mascot. Ask why. Vote for one. Write the winner and one reason.

title: Which Boring Job First?
text: Compare folding clothes, washing dishes and sorting books. Each defend doing one first. Agree on an order. Write the order and one reason.

title: What Makes a Good Question?
text: Compare “Do you like it?”, “Why?” and “What would you change?” Each explain when one helps. Write a useful situation for each question.

title: A Name Everyone Can Say
text: Each invent a name for a friendly alien. Say the names. Choose one that is easy to say. Write it and why you chose it.

title: The Best Small Surprise
text: Compare a funny note, a handmade badge and a favourite song. Each defend one as a surprise. Agree. Write your choice and who might enjoy it.

title: Useful, Funny or Beautiful?
text: Each choose what matters most in a gift: useful, funny or beautiful. Explain why. Design a gift combining two. Write the gift and the two qualities.

title: The Most Useful Question Word
text: Each defend who, how or why as the most useful question word. Give examples. Choose one for an interview. Write your choice and two example questions.

title: Can a Mistake Be Good?
text: Each invent a harmless mistake with a useful result. Compare them. Choose the best example. Write the mistake, result and what someone learned.

title: Same Result, Different Effort
text: Two imaginary teams finish equally well, but one practised more. Discuss what a fair judge should praise. Write your decision and two reasons.

title: Three Voices, One Rating
text: Invent a talking kettle. Each review one thing: usefulness, noise or fun. Agree on a rating from one to five. Write the rating and three comments.

title: Teach an Alien to Wave
text: Explain waving to an alien. Each add one short instruction. Check the order. Write three steps.

title: How to Ask to Join
text: Invent a friendly club. Each suggest one sentence a newcomer can say. Choose two useful sentences. Write them.

title: The Recipe with No Cooking
text: Invent a pretend snack needing no cooking. Each suggest an ingredient and a step. Agree. Write ingredients and three steps.

title: Explain Fair Turn-Taking
text: Explain taking turns to a pretend robot. Each suggest a rule. Test it with an example. Write three simple rules.

title: The Shorter Explanation
text: Explain how to choose a team name. Each gives one step. Remove repeated ideas. Write the instructions in thirty words or fewer.

title: Questions Before Directions
text: Someone says “How do I start?” Invent what they want to start. Each ask a useful question. Write the situation and your three questions.

title: Teach a Made-Up Greeting
text: Invent a greeting for imaginary visitors. Each add a word or action. Agree on a simple version. Write what people say and do.

title: Explain Without the Hard Word
text: Choose “fragile”, “patient” or “generous”. Each explain it using easier words. Combine the best ideas. Write one explanation and an example.

title: The Missing Step Test
text: Invent instructions for sending a pretend invitation. Leave out one important step. The others find it. Write the complete steps and mark the added one.

title: One Example Beats a Paragraph
text: Choose a simple idea like sharing or taking turns. Each invent an example. Pick the clearest. Write the idea and your example.

title: Three Words, One Sentence
text: Each choose a simple word. Say your words. Work together to put all three in one sensible sentence. Write the words and sentence.

title: The Friendly Alliteration Name
text: Each suggest an adjective and animal starting with the same letter. Say the names. Choose one. Write the name and a sentence about it.

title: One Object, Three Adjectives
text: Choose an everyday object. Each give a different adjective. Check that they fit. Write the object and three adjectives.

title: Our Opposite Mini-Story
text: Each suggest a pair of opposites. Use two pairs in a tiny story. Help each other connect it. Write the story. Mark opposite words with CAPITALS.

title: What Belongs in Our Category?
text: Invent a category, like soft things. Each give an example. Ask why it fits. Write the category and three examples.

title: The Word with Two Jobs
text: Choose “light”, “watch” or “ring”. Discuss two meanings. Each suggest a sentence. Write two sentences showing different meanings.

title: Build a Better Question
text: Start with “Do you like music?” Each suggest a more interesting question. Choose two. Write them and explain what they could reveal.

title: Explain Our New Saying
text: Invent a funny saying about patience or teamwork. Each explain what it could mean. Agree on one meaning. Write the saying and explanation.

title: The Sentence Rescue Team
text: Fix “Yesterday we go shop and buy three apple.” Each explain one correction. Agree on a clear sentence. Write it and one explanation.

title: Our Four-Line Sound Poem
text: Choose rain, wind or footsteps. Each suggest a sound word. Build a four-line poem together. Write it; rhymes are optional.

title: Because Is Not the End
text: Say “This is the best sandwich.” Each ask a question that checks the claim. Invent answers. Write the sandwich and one convincing reason.

title: A Fact or a Favourite?
text: Compare “Bananas are yellow” and “Bananas are the best snack.” Discuss which describes a fact and which gives an opinion. Write the difference and your examples.

title: The Amazing Blanket Claim
text: A pretend advert says a blanket makes everyone happy. Each ask a question. Agree on a more honest claim. Write it and one question you asked.

title: Evidence for the Best Cushion
text: Choose a pretend cushion. Each suggest a way to check if it is comfortable. Pick two checks. Write them and what you would look for.

title: Popular Does Not Explain It
text: An imaginary club chooses a game because it is popular. Each ask a question about whether it suits the group. Write three questions.

title: Maybe There Is Another Reason
text: An imaginary friend leaves a game early. Each suggest a harmless possible reason. Write three possibilities using “Maybe…”

title: The Fair Test for a Bag
text: Two pretend bags claim to be stronger. Discuss how to compare them fairly. Write a test and two things to keep the same.

title: Which Detail Would Help?
text: A message says “The box is missing.” Each ask for a useful detail. Choose three questions. Write them.

title: A Reason That Fits
text: Choose a quiet activity for an imaginary tired friend. Each offer a reason. Check which fits the friend’s need. Write the activity and best reason.

title: What Would Change Your Mind?
text: Choose between a tiny or huge imaginary house. Each explain a preference. Ask what could change it. Write two views and what might change each.

title: Everyone Adds One Welcome
text: Each suggest one friendly sentence for a new group member. Choose three sentences that work together. Write your welcome message.

title: A Fair Speaking Rule
text: Discuss how to stop one person doing all the talking. Each suggest a rule. Agree on one. Write the rule and how you know it is working.

title: Different Ideas, Shared Name
text: Each suggest a name for an imaginary team. Combine parts of your ideas. Write the new name and explain its parts.

title: One Thanks for Each Job
text: Imagine you made a poster together. Each invent one job they did. Thank each other. Write a thank-you sentence for each job.

title: The Quiet Member Invitation
text: Imagine a member has not spoken yet. Each suggest a gentle invitation to join. Choose two. Write them without pressuring the person.

title: The Job Nobody Wants
text: Your imaginary club needs someone to tidy up. Each suggest a fair way to share the job. Agree. Write your rule and why it helps.

title: Ask Before You Change It
text: A team member wants to change a shared design. Practise asking, responding and agreeing. Write a three-line exchange showing everyone gets a say.

title: A Good Group Restart
text: Imagine your group has talked for ages without choosing. Each suggest one next step. Agree on a reset plan. Write three short steps.

title: Keep the Idea, Change the Plan
text: Your pretend group wants a huge show but has little time. Each suggest what to keep or simplify. Agree. Write the core idea and two simplifications.

title: Our Best Team Habit
text: Each suggest one habit that makes group work easier. Ask for an example. Choose one to try. Write the habit and a situation where it helps.
